Hi Rajesh — great questions. Summary and proposed plan below.

High-level: we recommend a three-week technical sprint for the access controls track with a staged cutover across two windows (pilot -> broad). This keeps blast radius small and gives legal time to review exceptions.

Sprint cadence (proposal):
- Week 0 (prep): finalize SAML attribute map, SCIM field map, service-account names, and IP ranges.
- Week 1 (pilot): configure SAML + SCIM in staging, provision pilot OUs (~100 users), validate assertion fields and SCIM deltas.
- Week 2 (hardening): update mappings based on pilot results, create service-account runbook, add KV/cache ACL checks.
- Week 3 (cutover): rolling production syncers in 2 waves (50% / 50%) with a 24-hour pause between waves.

Exception approval matrix (attached):
- Emergency IP exceptions (short-lived, <=72 hours): CS on-call approves; legal notified within 24 hours.
- Permanent IP additions: Formal ticket + legal signoff; target SLA 5 business days.
- Service-account creation outside pattern: Requires engineering + security approval; may require temporary scoped access for 7 days.

Canary sizing: start with 100 pilot users in staging, then 500 users in the first prod wave. If SCIM error rate <0.5% and SAML assertions validated, proceed to second wave.

Notes on SAML/SCIM specifics:
- SAML: we'll map email -> NameID (transient), plus groups -> role claim. We recommend including the full orgUnitPath in the assertion to avoid post-sync role recompute.
- SCIM: use incremental delta sync; we'll share a sample scim-field-map (attached).
- Service accounts: pattern doc attached explains naming convention (acme-syncer-<env>-<region>) and key rotation cadence (90 days).

Deliverables by end of Week 0: scim-field-map, IP allowlist spreadsheet with CIDR windows, service-account runbook, approval matrix.

I've attached three quick artifacts (spreadsheet + runbook + example scim map). Ben and Monica will pick up the staging config and the runbook respectively.

Next steps: please confirm the go/no-go for the pilot window (we're proposing pilot start 2026-12-06) and whether legal needs any additional artifacts for the permanent IP request path.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Adding a couple of technical constraints and a checklist for the pilot:

Technical notes:
- SCIM: we'll run delta sync every 30m for pilot, switch to 15m after cutover if errors <=0.2%.
- SAML: require a persistent audience value and a clock skew tolerance of 120s to accommodate their IdP appliances.
- IP allowlist: recommend staged CIDR expansion with sticky sessions enabled on the load balancer; otherwise KV cache mismatch can cause auth failures.

Pilot checklist (staging):
- Confirm SAML cert fingerprint with IdP team.
- Deploy staging syncer container with service-account acme-syncer-stg-1.
- Run dry-run SCIM delete detection and export results to Drive.
- Smoke test app login and role mapping with 3 users across 2 OUs.

I can own the staging syncer deploy and the dry-run artifacts. Kimberly — can you own the legal-facing exception matrix signoff and Monica the service-account created/applied steps? I put tentative owner assignments in the attached spreadsheet.

-ben
